risk_register.description: If Workday API integration requires custom field mapping, custom configuration, or sandbox is unavailable, then Phase 2 integration work extends 2–4 weeks, delaying IT account provisioning and document pre-population features.
risk_register.trigger: Workday API sandbox unavailable, documentation incomplete, or custom field mapping required during Phase 2 sprint kickoff
risk_register.mitigation: Confirm Workday API sandbox access, review API documentation, and validate standard employee data export scope in week 1 discovery; establish fallback to manual data entry if API unavailable
risk_register.contingency: If API unavailable or requires custom work, pivot to manual data entry for Phase 2 or extend timeline 2–4 weeks; escalate to Workday account manager for sandbox restoration

risk_register.description: If Azure AD provisioning API requires custom scripting, SCIM integrations lack support for Slack/SaaS tools, or IT Administrator lacks automation experience, then Phase 2 integration extends 3–6 weeks, blocking 'zero manual tickets' success metric.
risk_register.trigger: Azure AD provisioning API documentation gaps, Slack/SaaS tools lack SCIM support, or IT Administrator reports unfamiliarity with Azure AD automation during Phase 1
risk_register.mitigation: Conduct hands-on Azure AD provisioning proof-of-concept in Phase 1; confirm SCIM support for all target SaaS tools; pair IT Administrator with Backend Developer for automation scripting; document provisioning workflow before Phase 2 sprint
risk_register.contingency: If custom scripting required, allocate Backend Developer capacity away from portal UI or extend Phase 2 timeline 3–6 weeks; if SCIM unavailable, implement manual provisioning workflow or reduce scope to email-only

risk_register.description: If e-signature service is not pre-selected or forms require legal/compliance redesign, then Phase 1 extends 1–3 weeks for vendor evaluation, legal review, and form redesign, compressing Phase 2 timeline.
risk_register.trigger: E-signature vendor not confirmed in week 1, or legal/compliance review identifies form redesign requirements during Phase 1
risk_register.mitigation: Confirm e-signature service selection and API documentation before Phase 1 kickoff; schedule legal/compliance review of I-9/W-4/direct deposit forms in week 1; pre-approve form templates with legal team
risk_register.contingency: If vendor selection delayed, conduct parallel vendor evaluation in Phase 1 week 1; if forms require redesign, allocate UX Designer capacity and extend Phase 1 by 1–2 weeks

risk_register.description: If IT account provisioning scope is undefined (email-only vs. Slack/SaaS/VPN), then Phase 2 integration scope may expand unexpectedly, causing scope creep and timeline slip.
risk_register.trigger: Stakeholder requests additional SaaS tool provisioning during Phase 2, or IT Administrator identifies undocumented provisioning requirements
risk_register.mitigation: Define and document complete IT account provisioning scope (email, Slack, SaaS tools, VPN) in Phase 1 week 1; obtain written stakeholder sign-off on provisioning scope before Phase 2 sprint planning
risk_register.contingency: If scope expands, invoke change control process; prioritize email and Slack as MVP, defer additional SaaS tools to Phase 3 or post-launch

risk_register.description: If Product Owner is not designated or lacks authority for backlog prioritization and trade-off decisions, then Hybrid SDLC sprint cycles will experience decision bottlenecks, delaying sprint execution and Phase 2–3 delivery.
risk_register.trigger: Product Owner not named in project charter, or PO reports to multiple stakeholders without clear decision authority
risk_register.mitigation: Designate single Product Owner with explicit authority for backlog prioritization and trade-off decisions before Phase 2 kickoff; establish PO availability commitment (minimum 10 hours/week); document PO escalation path for stakeholder conflicts
risk_register.contingency: If PO unavailable, escalate to project sponsor for interim decision authority; implement daily standup to surface blockers requiring PO decision

risk_register.description: If team lacks hands-on experience with React/Node.js stack or Azure AD SSO integration, then Phase 2 development velocity may be lower than estimated, extending timeline or reducing feature scope.
risk_register.trigger: Backend or Frontend Developer reports unfamiliarity with React/Node.js during Phase 1, or SSO integration spike reveals unexpected complexity
risk_register.mitigation: Conduct React/Node.js and Azure AD SSO proof-of-concept in Phase 1 week 1–2; allocate 2–3 days for team ramp-up on stack; pair junior developer with senior contractor if needed
risk_register.contingency: If velocity lower than estimated, reduce Phase 2 feature scope or extend timeline; escalate to PM for resource augmentation (contractor developer)

risk_register.description: If SOC 2 compliance requirements are not fully scoped (audit log retention, data handling controls, encryption), then Phase 2 development may require rework post-launch, delaying compliance certification.
risk_register.trigger: Security/compliance review in Phase 1 identifies missing audit log controls, data retention policy undefined, or encryption requirements not implemented
risk_register.mitigation: Schedule security/compliance review in Phase 1 week 1; define audit log retention policy (e.g., 7 years for I-9), data handling controls, and encryption requirements before Phase 2 sprint planning; document SOC 2 control mapping
risk_register.contingency: If compliance gaps identified post-Phase 2, allocate Backend Developer capacity for remediation; delay launch until compliance certification achieved

risk_register.description: If any critical path role (PM, Backend Developer, Frontend Developer) becomes unavailable or is pulled to competing priorities, then project timeline will slip or scope will be reduced.
risk_register.trigger: PM, Backend Developer, or Frontend Developer reports competing project allocation, illness, or departure during Phase 2–3
risk_register.mitigation: Secure written commitment from resource managers that PM, Backend Developer, and Frontend Developer are 100% dedicated to project through Phase 5; establish escalation path if resource contention arises; cross-train UX Designer on basic backend tasks as backup
risk_register.contingency: If critical resource unavailable, escalate to project sponsor for replacement or timeline extension; activate contingency contractor if available

risk_register.description: If Phase 1 discovery (vendor selection, scope definition, compliance review) extends beyond 4 weeks, then Phase 2–3 timeline compresses, increasing execution risk and quality defects.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 1 discovery activities (e-signature vendor selection, Workday/Azure AD API validation, compliance review) not completed by end of week 4
risk_register.mitigation: Establish Phase 1 discovery milestones (vendor selection by week 2, API validation by week 3, compliance review by week 4); assign PM to track discovery blockers daily; escalate delays immediately
risk_register.contingency: If Phase 1 extends, compress Phase 2 timeline by reducing feature scope or extending overall project deadline

risk_register.description: If data retention policy for onboarding documents and audit logs is not defined before Phase 2, then database schema and compliance controls may require re-architecture post-launch.
risk_register.trigger: Data retention policy not documented in Phase 1, or compliance review identifies retention gaps during Phase 2 development
risk_register.mitigation: Define data retention policy (e.g., 7 years for I-9, 3 years for audit logs) in Phase 1 week 1; document retention requirements in database schema design; validate retention controls with compliance team before Phase 2 sprint
risk_register.contingency: If retention policy undefined post-Phase 2, implement data archival/deletion logic in Phase 3 or post-launch; conduct compliance re-review

risk_register.description: If external API rate limiting (Workday, Azure AD, e-signature service) is not validated during Phase 1, then production onboarding workflows may fail during peak new hire periods (e.g., quarterly hiring cycles).
risk_register.trigger: API rate limits not documented in Phase 1, or load testing in Phase 4 reveals rate limit violations during peak onboarding periods
risk_register.mitigation: Document API rate limits for Workday, Azure AD, and e-signature service in Phase 1; conduct load testing in Phase 4 to validate rate limit handling; implement request queuing/throttling if needed
risk_register.contingency: If rate limits exceeded in production, implement exponential backoff retry logic or request quota increase from API vendor

risk_register.description: If 'nice to have' features (chat with HR bot, mobile app, LMS integration) are not formally deprioritized, then stakeholder expectations may creep into MVP scope, compressing Phase 2 timeline.
risk_register.trigger: Stakeholder requests 'nice to have' features during Phase 2 sprint planning, or Product Owner includes them in MVP backlog without explicit trade-off discussion
risk_register.mitigation: Formally document 'nice to have' features as Phase 3+ backlog in Phase 1; obtain written stakeholder sign-off that MVP excludes chat bot, mobile app, and LMS integration; establish change control process for scope additions
risk_register.contingency: If stakeholder insists on 'nice to have' features, invoke change control; prioritize features and extend timeline or reduce other scope
